key_insight: For silicon spin quantum computers, the lowest temperature is not always the most energy-efficient: an optimal finite operating temperature balances cryogenic cooling power against rising error-correction overhead at higher temperatures.
engineering_relevance: This work provides a system-level design rule for scalable silicon quantum processors by linking device fidelity limits to total power consumption and cooling infrastructure.
method: Benchmark two-qubit silicon chips from industrial and academic fabrication with gate set tomography.
Measure coherence, gate fidelity, and state-preparation-and-measurement errors across a temperature range.
Combine the observed error trends with a cryogenic cooling plus error-correction power model.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports elevated temperatures shorten coherence times and worsen gate/SPAM infidelities, with a sharp fidelity crossover near 1 K in current devices.
watch_item: The optimal temperature depends on present device performance, so the crossover near 1 K may shift as qubit materials, control, and error-correction schemes improve.
paper_title: Optimal operating temperature for industry-compatible silicon spin quantum computing: colder is not necessarily better
